reason: The spool is turned and six-fold symmetric about its axis (a six-hole circle at 60° pitch on one end, twelve-hole circles at 30° on both flanges). The anchors distinctive enough to align by all lie on the axis; the off-axis repeats (holes, chamfers and their faces) then vote for the turn about it, and six turns fit them equally (alignment.fold 6, symmetric set). Which copy is which is undetermined by the geometry, so, as for any symmetric part, the turn giving the motion nearest the identity is taken and every off-axis feature and face is carried, consistently, onto its image under that turn: here a 30° turn rather than the motion's own, so the 48 pre-existing off-axis features and 72 faces land on their symmetric copies. Under translate, rot_x90 and rot_y180 the identity-nearest turn is the motion's own and everything is carried to itself. For #127, the six new concave R40 web fillets follow the same face permutation. The exact 72-face ambiguity is unchanged, and the invariance test additionally requires all six fillets to be Carried consistently with the face map. For #127, after #128 claims the six concave web rounds, the six residual convex R10 profiles follow the same permutation (54 features total). All 48 main feature IDs, including its six fillets, and the exact 72-face assertion are retained; the test requires the profiles to be Carried consistently with the face map.

Remaining absolute publication-grid effect: SectionRecessGeometry requires its run_interval endpoints on a three-decimal grid about a frame origin perpendicular to the run. On mfcadpp/10170 the independently rounded endpoints give run lengths 23.209 mm unmoved and 23.210 mm translated (also under rot_zx_moved), on the same faces. Local section side and opening sizes are now placement-independent; this interval needs a versioned intrinsic run-length representation or an along-run frame origin. The recogniser publication is wrong here, not correspondence; frozen Python shares it. tests/invariance.rs continues to pin this exact case.
